thread:
maya (PM): heads-up — ACME asked for a self-serve view of their reserved pool/quota and burst credits. they want something customer-facing in Console before GA. can we scope a minimal spec?

alex (Eng): agree this helps reduce support. what are the must-haves vs nice-to-haves?

maya (PM): must-haves: current reserved pool usage (tokens/min and tokens/day), remaining burst credits, next reset time, and a simple explainer of what burst means. nice-to-have: historical trend, forecasted exhaustion warning, and a request button to top-up.

sam (SRE): must-have for us: accurate live usage that matches billing so customers aren't confused. we should surface a 5m and 1h aggregated metric, and an opaque ID for debugging. also rate-limit the dashboard queries.

leo (Design): can mock a compact widget that fits into the Console's account page. idea: three vertical tiles — "Reserved usage", "Burst balance", "Alerts". minimal copy and microcopy for terms. will attach a lo-fi. :+1:

jen (Sales): ACME cares about being able to prove to their finance team consumption at month-end. if we can export CSV or link to billing, that'd be huge for closing. also they asked for an API endpoint.

alex (Eng): exporting CSV + API is additional work but doable. timeline question: is this for GA or post-GA?

maya (PM): ask came up in onboarding pilot — they'd prefer before contract signing if possible. compromise: GA-lite — Console widget + CSV export. API and forecast as follow-ups.

sam (SRE): operational constraints: we can't run expensive per-tenant joins on every page load. propose cached materialized view that updates every 60s and an on-demand rehydrate for owners. also need a permission check to avoid leaking other tenants.

alex (Eng): sounds reasonable. implementation sketch: 1) new aggregated metrics table by tenant with fields {tenant_id, reserved_tokens_1h, reserved_tokens_24h, burst_balance, next_reset_ts, last_synced_ts} 2) read endpoint that returns the tile payload and CSV. caching layer in front.

maya (PM): can you paste the mock API response we'd show the Console? we can use that in UX microcopy.

alex (Eng): sure —

```
GET /api/v1/tenants/:id/quota-view
200 OK
{
  "tenant_id": "acme",
  "reserved_tokens_1h": 12450,
  "reserved_tokens_24h": 312000,
  "burst_balance": 18000,
  "next_reset_ts": 1746316800,
  "last_synced_ts": 1746224400
}
```

leo (Design): nice. for the tile copy i suggest: "Reserved pool: 12.45k / 100k last 1h" and "Burst credits: 18k (resets 2025-06-02)". add a tooltip: "Burst credits are temporary tokens applied when reserved capacity is exceeded."

jen (Sales): can we add a footnote: "CSV export includes timestamps + per-route breakdown" — ACME will want per-route for internal chargeback.

sam (SRE): per-route data gets big. add an admin-only flag to enable detailed breakdown for accounts that request it. falls back to aggregated view otherwise.

maya (PM): prioritization ask: we have 2 weeks before ACME contract milestone. propose MLP scope: Console tiles + CSV export + permission gating + tests + basic docs. stretch: one-click request-to-top-up (which triggers a sales flow).

alex (Eng): estimate: 6 dev-weeks for MLP (eng + infra + API + UI + CSV). 2 more weeks for opt-in per-route breakdown and admin controls.

leo (Design): 1.5 designer-weeks for final mocks, copy, and accessibility checks.

jen (Sales): is there a risk this delays the contract? if we can't hit the 2-week milestone should we ship a beta link to ACME with a manual CSV in the interim?

maya (PM): good point. fallback plan: manual CSV + scheduled sync and a simple screenshot from Console prototype. we should offer an "ACME pilot" whitelist to give them early access once backend exists.

sam (SRE): security checklist: tenant scoping, audit log entry when CSV exported, rate limits, and opt-in for detailed traces. I'll add a short runbook.

alex (Eng): blockers: 1) a stable aggregation pipeline (we can reuse existing billing aggregator for numbers), 2) who owns the CSV export format (billing vs product).

maya (PM): i'll own product spec + acceptance criteria. jen can own the customer communications for the pilot. alex — can you validate reuse of billing aggregator by EOD Friday?

alex (Eng): will do. if reuse works, cut in half the engineering time estimate.

ops-bot: Deployment pipeline: analytics-aggregator service build #482 succeeded at 1746224300.

maya (PM): action items: alex validate aggregator, leo start lo-fi -> hi-fi, sam draft security checklist, jen coordinate ACME expectation, i'll write acceptance criteria and add to roadmap.

leo (Design): attaching lo-fi in #design later today.

jen (Sales): i'll update ACME and ask if CSV will unblock them ASAP.

alex (Eng): quick Q re: "forecasted exhaustion" — do we want a simple threshold alert (e.g. <20% burst left) in MLP or save for follow-up?

maya (PM): save for follow-up unless ACME insists. keep MLP focused.

sam (SRE): ack. adding alerting as follow-up ticket.

maya (PM): thanks all. if anyone has major objections call out now, otherwise i'll create the spec doc and roadmap ticket with the MLP scope. :rocket:
